ALL_NULL.purpose: Every column is NULL except id, embedding (a fixed-size list is never NULL: it holds 32 NULL elements instead) and all_empty_list ([]).

EMPTIES.purpose: Empty values: [] for lists, {} for maps, structs whose fields are all NULL, '' and an empty blob for top-level text and BLOB, {} for JSON documents, and an all-zero embedding.

NULL_ELEMENTS.purpose: NULL inside values: list elements ([4, NULL, 17]), map values, struct fields, a NULL inner list, a NULL struct in people, JSON null members, and SQL NULL next to the JSON literal null in json_list.

NUMERIC_EXTREMES.purpose: Numeric edges: 2^53-1 and 2^53+1, INT64 min and max, UINT64 max, the decimals [1.25, 2.50, 3.75], DECIMAL(38,0) max, and NaN, +-Infinity, -0.0 and 5e-324 in doubles; INT8/INT16/INT32 bounds and float32 edges in the narrower columns.

TEXT_ESCAPES.purpose: Text that needs quoting or escaping: it's, "dq", a, b, [x], k=v, the text NULL, '', two single quotes, a backslash, a newline, a tab, right-to-left text and combining marks, as list elements, map keys, struct fields and JSON strings.

LIST_1000.purpose: long_list and tags hold 1,000 items (long_list holds 1..1000), int_keys holds 600 entries, and doc is a 1,000-item JSON array; the JSON file's counts holds 1,000 digits.

LIST_2500.purpose: long_list and tags hold 2,500 items (long_list holds 1..2500), as does the JSON file's counts; doc is the JSON scalar 42.

LIST_10000.purpose: long_list and tags hold 10,000 items (long_list holds 1..10000), as does the JSON file's counts; doc is the JSON literal null.

CAP_EDGE.purpose: The display cap: strings_edge (and the JSON file's words) holds one 20,000-character element and tags holds three, each placing the ZWJ family emoji (7 code points, 11 UTF-16 units) at code points 998-1004 of the DuckDB cell text, so a 1000-code-point or -UTF-16-unit cut would split it while a 1000-grapheme cut keeps it whole; raw_blob holds 300 bytes; wide_struct renders past 1000 characters; doc holds the long string.

DATE_BINARY_EDGES.purpose: Date and binary edges: 0001-01-01, 9999-12-31, 1970-01-01 and a pre-1970 date (dates, timestamps, map keys, struct leaves), the nil and all-ones UUIDs, and blobs that are empty or hold \x00, \xff and quote/backslash bytes.

DEMO.purpose: Readable values for demos and docs: tags [red, green, blue], point {x: 1.5, y: -0.5, tier: gold}, a contact card in nested_struct, two people, and int_keys with keys 2, 1, 10 in that order.

NAME_COLLISIONS.purpose: Keys whose extracted default column names collide: doc holds the JSON keys a.b, a_b and A_B, attrs (and the JSON file's props) the map keys k=v, k_v and K_V next to size, toJSON, constructor, __proto__, 2 and 1.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Row number 0-999; equals the __rowid__ the loaders add.

columns.name: label
columns.description: Showcase rows: their name; other rows: a random two-word label.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: About 250 characters of stock sentences.

columns.name: raw_blob
columns.description: Top-level BLOB, 0-16 bytes; 300 bytes in the CAP_EDGE row.

columns.name: tags
columns.description: 1-8 short words; 1,000 / 2,500 / 10,000 words in rows 5-7.

columns.name: scores
columns.description: 1-10 integers 0-100.

columns.name: long_list
columns.description: 1-40 integers 0-99 (longer than the 32-item preview in a fifth of the rows); 1..1000, 1..2500 and 1..10000 in rows 5-7.

columns.name: matrix
columns.description: A list of 1-4 lists of 0-4 SMALLINTs.

columns.name: deep_list
columns.description: Three levels of lists of TINYINTs.

columns.name: embedding
columns.description: A fixed-size list of 32 FLOATs with two decimals, -1 to 1 (DuckDB reads it as FLOAT[]); never NULL: 32 NULL elements in ALL_NULL, zeros in EMPTIES, float32 edges in NUMERIC_EXTREMES.

columns.name: doubles
columns.description: 1-4 DOUBLEs at full precision; NaN, +-Infinity, -0.0, 5e-324 and +-DOUBLE max in NUMERIC_EXTREMES.

columns.name: decimals
columns.description: 1-5 DECIMAL(10,2)s; [1.25, 2.50, 3.75] in NUMERIC_EXTREMES, which bridge.query used to return as [6.2e-322, 0, 1.235e-321].

columns.name: big_ints
columns.description: 1-3 BIGINTs within +-2^62 (most beyond 2^53); 2^53+-1 and INT64 bounds in NUMERIC_EXTREMES.

columns.name: ubig
columns.description: 1-3 UBIGINTs over the whole range; UINT64 max in NUMERIC_EXTREMES.

columns.name: timestamps_tz
columns.description: 1-2 TIMESTAMPTZs 1990-2029 with microseconds; the range ends and the epoch in DATE_BINARY_EDGES.

columns.name: times
columns.description: 1-2 TIMEs with microseconds.

columns.name: uuids
columns.description: 1-3 version-4 UUIDs from a pool of 32 (Parquet UUID logical type); the nil and all-ones UUIDs in DATE_BINARY_EDGES.

columns.name: blobs
columns.description: 1-3 BLOBs of 0-6 bytes.

columns.name: bools
columns.description: 1-6 BOOLEANs.

columns.name: strings_edge
columns.description: 1-5 strings, half of them needing quotes or escapes; every escape case in TEXT_ESCAPES; one 20,000-character element in CAP_EDGE.

columns.name: tier_list
columns.description: Cycles through 8 lists by row number (row % 8) whose texts pair up as look-alikes: [NULL] (a NULL element) and ['NULL'] (the text NULL), [] and [''], ['a, b'] and [a, b]; NULL in ALL_NULL.

columns.name: point
columns.arrowType: struct<x: double, y: double, tier: string>
columns.duckdbType: STRUCT(x DOUBLE, y DOUBLE, tier VARCHAR)
columns.description: STRUCT(x, y, tier): the shape of the wide test file's struct columns; x and y normal with two decimals, tier bronze/silver/gold/platinum.

columns.name: odd_names
columns.arrowType: struct<label: string, name: string, type: string, data: string, size: int32, length: int32, toJSON: string, constructor: string, __proto__: string, hasOwnProperty: bool, months: int32, days: int32, nanoseconds: int64, my field: string, x,y: double, quote"d: string, it's: string, 2: int32, 1: int32, 10: int32, ünï: string, emoji😀: string, order: int32, null: string, SELECT: string, ID: int64>
columns.duckdbType: STRUCT("label" VARCHAR, "name" VARCHAR, "type" VARCHAR, "data" VARCHAR, size INTEGER, length INTEGER, toJSON VARCHAR, constructor VARCHAR, __proto__ VARCHAR, hasOwnProperty BOOLEAN, "months" INTEGER, "days" INTEGER, nanoseconds BIGINT, "my field" VARCHAR, "x,y" DOUBLE, "quote""d" VARCHAR, "it's" VARCHAR, "2" INTEGER, "1" INTEGER, "10" INTEGER, "ünï" VARCHAR, "emoji😀" VARCHAR, "order" INTEGER, "null" VARCHAR, "SELECT" VARCHAR, ID BIGINT)
columns.description: 26 fields named label, name, type, data, size, length, toJSON, constructor, __proto__, hasOwnProperty, months, days, nanoseconds, "my field", "x,y", quote"d, it's, 2, 1, 10, ünï, emoji😀, order, null, SELECT, ID: names that break JavaScript objects or need SQL quoting.

columns.name: typed_leaves
columns.arrowType: struct<dec38: decimal128(38, 0), dec18_4: decimal128(18, 4), uuid: extension<arrow.uuid>, blob: binary, time: time64[us], ts: timestamp[us], tstz: timestamp[us, tz=UTC], date: date32[day], flag: bool, f32: float, i64: int64>
columns.duckdbType: STRUCT(dec38 DECIMAL(38,0), dec18_4 DECIMAL(18,4), uuid UUID, blob BLOB, "time" TIME, ts TIMESTAMP, tstz TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, date DATE, flag BOOLEAN, f32 FLOAT, i64 BIGINT)
columns.description: One leaf of each type that has gone wrong inside a nested value: DECIMAL(38,0), DECIMAL(18,4), UUID, BLOB, TIME, TIMESTAMP, TIMESTAMPTZ, DATE, BOOLEAN, FLOAT, BIGINT.

columns.name: wide_struct
columns.arrowType: struct<f01: int32, f02: double, f03: string, f04: bool, f05: date32[day], f06: int64, f07: float, f08: int16, f09: int32, f10: double, f11: string, f12: bool, f13: date32[day], f14: int64, f15: float, f16: int16, f17: int32, f18: double, f19: string, f20: bool, f21: date32[day], f22: int64, f23: float, f24: int16, f25: int32, f26: double, f27: string, f28: bool, f29: date32[day], f30: int64, f31: float, f32: int16, f33: int32, f34: double, f35: string, f36: bool, f37: date32[day], f38: int64, f39: float, f40: int16>
columns.duckdbType: STRUCT(f01 INTEGER, f02 DOUBLE, f03 VARCHAR, f04 BOOLEAN, f05 DATE, f06 BIGINT, f07 FLOAT, f08 SMALLINT, f09 INTEGER, f10 DOUBLE, f11 VARCHAR, f12 BOOLEAN, f13 DATE, f14 BIGINT, f15 FLOAT, f16 SMALLINT, f17 INTEGER, f18 DOUBLE, f19 VARCHAR, f20 BOOLEAN, f21 DATE, f22 BIGINT, f23 FLOAT, f24 SMALLINT, f25 INTEGER, f26 DOUBLE, f27 VARCHAR, f28 BOOLEAN, f29 DATE, f30 BIGINT, f31 FLOAT, f32 SMALLINT, f33 INTEGER, f34 DOUBLE, f35 VARCHAR, f36 BOOLEAN, f37 DATE, f38 BIGINT, f39 FLOAT, f40 SMALLINT)
columns.description: 40 scalar fields f01-f40 cycling INTEGER, DOUBLE, VARCHAR, BOOLEAN, DATE, BIGINT, FLOAT, SMALLINT; its CAP_EDGE row (150-character strings) renders past 1,000 characters.

columns.name: nested_struct
columns.arrowType: struct<owner: struct<name: string, contact: struct<email: string, phones: list<item: string>, address: struct<city: string, zip: string>>>, version: int32>
columns.duckdbType: STRUCT("owner" STRUCT("name" VARCHAR, contact STRUCT(email VARCHAR, phones VARCHAR[], address STRUCT(city VARCHAR, zip VARCHAR))), "version" INTEGER)
columns.description: Four levels deep: owner.contact.address.city, with owner.contact.email and the list owner.contact.phones.

columns.name: people
columns.arrowType: list<item: struct<name: string, age: int32, langs: list<item: string>>>
columns.duckdbType: STRUCT("name" VARCHAR, age INTEGER, langs VARCHAR[])[]
columns.description: A list of 1-4 STRUCT(name, age, langs VARCHAR[]).

columns.name: attrs
columns.description: 1-5 keys drawn from size, toJSON, constructor, __proto__, 2, 1, k=v, length and ordinary names; escape cases as keys in TEXT_ESCAPES.

columns.name: int_keys
columns.description: 1-5 INTEGER keys -100..100; 600 entries in LIST_1000; keys 2, 1, 10 in that order in DEMO.

columns.name: date_keys
columns.description: 1-3 DATE keys 2020-2025, each mapped to a list of 0-3 integers.

columns.name: map_of_structs
columns.arrowType: map<string, struct<qty: int32, price: decimal128(10, 2), note: string>>
columns.duckdbType: MAP(VARCHAR, STRUCT(qty INTEGER, price DECIMAL(10,2), note VARCHAR))
columns.description: 1-3 fruit keys mapped to STRUCT(qty INTEGER, price DECIMAL(10,2), note VARCHAR).

columns.name: doc
columns.description: JSON documents (Parquet JSON logical type) with keys k, score, kind, "my field", "a.b", q"k, ünï; some rows a JSON scalar, an array or the literal null (a 1,000-item array, 42 and null in rows 5-7).

columns.name: json_list
columns.description: A list of 1-2 JSON values (objects, arrays, scalars, the literal null); SQL NULL next to the JSON literal null in NULL_ELEMENTS.

columns.name: all_null_list
columns.description: NULL in every row.

columns.name: all_empty_list
columns.description: [] in every row.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Row number 0-999; equals the __rowid__ the loader adds.

columns.name: label
columns.description: As the Parquet file's label.

columns.name: counts
columns.description: Non-negative integers (BIGINT[]); 1,000 / 2,500 / 10,000 single digits (position mod 10, to keep the file small) in rows 5-7.

columns.name: signed
columns.description: Integers of both signs: read_json infers HUGEINT[] for them, not BIGINT[] (it reads non-negative integers as unsigned).

columns.name: huge
columns.description: Non-negative integers, past INT64 max in NUMERIC_EXTREMES (2^63 and UINT64 max), which makes read_json infer HUGEINT[].

columns.name: floats
columns.description: DOUBLE[] with three decimals; NUMERIC_EXTREMES holds -0.0, 5e-324, +-DOUBLE max and 2^64 (an integer past UINT64, which read_json reads as a DOUBLE).

columns.name: words
columns.description: VARCHAR[]: 1-2 words; the escape cases in TEXT_ESCAPES; the 20,000-character element in CAP_EDGE.

columns.name: days
columns.description: ISO date strings, which read_json reads as DATE[].

columns.name: ids
columns.description: UUID strings, which read_json reads as UUID[].

columns.name: point
columns.duckdbType: STRUCT(x DOUBLE, y DOUBLE, tier VARCHAR)
columns.description: As the Parquet file's point; {} (read as all-NULL fields) in EMPTIES.

columns.name: depth5
columns.duckdbType: STRUCT(l2 STRUCT(l3 STRUCT(l4 STRUCT(l5 STRUCT(leaf BIGINT)))))
columns.description: A STRUCT five levels deep (the column, then l2, l3, l4, l5), with one leaf: depth5.l2.l3.l4.l5.leaf.

columns.name: props
columns.description: Objects whose keys vary from row to row (key_000-key_499, rarely size/toJSON/constructor/__proto__), which read_json reads as MAP(VARCHAR, BIGINT); a.b, a_b, A_B, k=v and k_v in NAME_COLLISIONS (case-colliding keys would fail as STRUCT fields).

columns.name: empty_list
columns.description: [] in every non-NULL row, which read_json reads as JSON[].

columns.name: mixed_list
columns.description: Arrays mixing numbers, strings, booleans, null, objects and arrays, which read_json reads as JSON[] (a JSON null element is SQL NULL).

columns.name: shifty
columns.description: A field whose type changes from row to row (number, string, boolean, object, array), which read_json reads as JSON.

columns.name: key_order
columns.description: An object whose key "2" comes before "1": STRUCT("2" BIGINT, "1" BIGINT), in that order.

columns.name: people
columns.duckdbType: STRUCT("name" VARCHAR, age BIGINT, langs VARCHAR[])[]
columns.description: A list of 1-2 objects {name, age, langs}: STRUCT(...)[], with "name" quoted in the DESCRIBE text (a keyword).

columns.name: odd_keys
columns.duckdbType: STRUCT(k VARCHAR, score DOUBLE, kind VARCHAR, "my field" JSON, "a.b" BIGINT, "q""k" BOOLEAN, "ünï" VARCHAR)
columns.description: Objects with the keys k, score, kind, "my field", "a.b", q"k and ünï (a random subset, in that order), read as a STRUCT whose field names need quoting; "my field" holds a number in some rows and text in others, so read_json types that field JSON.

columns.name: matrix
columns.description: Non-negative integer arrays of arrays (BIGINT[][]).

columns.name: all_null
columns.description: null in every row, which read_json reads as JSON.

columns.name: empty_obj
columns.description: {} in every non-NULL row, which read_json reads as MAP(VARCHAR, JSON).
